comparisons.nift: The same nift build command is used in development and production. It checks the graph and renders only affected pages; most edits do not wake Node or rebuild the island.
comparisons.astro: The framework build owns page generation, component compilation, integrations, and client assets together.

comparisons.nift: HTML templates and JSON own static structure. Ordinary JavaScript owns small interactions. React is constrained to animation lifecycle and coordinated showcase state.
comparisons.astro: Astro components organise the site and integrate React components through the framework’s island model.

comparisons.nift: One small native executable plus 30 Node lockfile entries for the optional React island bundle.
comparisons.astro: A familiar JavaScript toolchain with 794 lockfile entries and a much larger installed dependency tree.

comparisons.nift: @pathto turns page and asset relationships into checked build requirements, supplemented by a final-output audit.
comparisons.astro: Asset and route correctness comes from framework conventions, module imports, integrations, and whatever additional link checking the project configures.

comparisons.nift: A successful but crude prototype. Its repeated theme UI and route families are structured; more extracted HTML should still be refactored.
comparisons.astro: The established upstream implementation, with mature source organisation and production history.

comparisons.nift: A small model that is quick to inspect, but a smaller community and less accumulated team familiarity.
comparisons.astro: Broader familiarity, documentation, integrations, examples, and an existing pool of experienced developers.

ai_dx.title: Short feedback loops
ai_dx.text: A one-page edit rebuilt in roughly 0.15 seconds in the constrained container. Fast verification changes how often an agent can afford to check its work.

ai_dx.title: Explicit relationships
ai_dx.text: @input, @json, and @pathto state dependencies close to their use. The build can explain why a page is stale or reject a missing target.

ai_dx.title: Low context tax
ai_dx.text: The central model fits into a small mental map. Agents spend fewer tokens rediscovering framework lifecycle and configuration layers.

ai_dx.title: No immunity from mistakes
ai_dx.text: The agent still produced visual mismatches and JavaScript integration regressions. Nift made fixes cheap; it did not replace acceptance testing.

method.title: Match the actual scope
method.text: Both implementations were evaluated as complete 2,647-page sites. The first simplified-homepage attempt was rejected as an invalid comparison.

method.title: Restore visual and interactive behaviour
method.text: The homepage was iterated against the live Omarchy site, including its pixel hero, mouse interaction, theme showcase, music, and draggable rails.

method.title: Move structure into Nift
method.text: Homepage sections, redirect families, repeated theme data, and internal relationships were moved into templates, JSON, loops, inputs, and path contracts.

method.title: Measure warmed builds
method.text: Five runs were collected for each workflow and medians reported. Astro and the comparable Nift production build ran in the same constrained environment.

method.title: Validate the output
method.text: Nift status confirmed every tracked page current, while an independent audit resolved local HTML, CSS, and JavaScript references against generated files.
